name: Lake Titicaca
blurb: Lake Titicaca is a high-altitude lake situated in the Andes mountains along the border of Peru and Bolivia. It is home to unique local wildlife, including the flightless Titicaca grebe and the aquatic Lake Titicaca frog.

positive: Enjoyable train journeys and scenic views
Fascinating local wildlife and natural history
Memorable visits to small islands and weaver communities
negative: Declining water levels leading to concerns as a threatened lake
Ongoing pollution problems in the area

quotes.text:
2/ "overages" go through a small "outlet" river. 
Sadly, its water level has declined to the point that some conservationists (the good kind) have started calling it a "threatened lake". There's also been pollution problems.
But, for right now, Lake Titicaca is an actual lake :)

This is the Titicaca Grebe. Found only on Lake Titicaca and in the surrounding areas.  It is completely flightless! Mind you, if you can run on water at that speed, who cares?

Titicaca National Reserve (est. 1978) in Peru protects a unique biome of over 60 bird species, 18 amphibians & varied mammals. It is famed for the endemic, critically-endangered Titicaca giant frog & the flightless Titicaca grebe; alongside Andean foxes, vizcachas & vast totora reed beds.

Here are some of my photos from my last trip to Lake Titicaca (from Puno, #Peru). I'm not a spiritual kind of man, but there's something about Titicaca that gets right inside me, especially out on the small islands where the master weavers live. If you ever get the chance, go.
